newsitem.title: USA: Magellan, Crescent in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Magellan, Crescent in joint venture.

text.p: Magellan Health Services Inc., the largest U.S. integrated behavioural health care company, said Thursday it will receive at least $400 million in a joint venture deal with Crescent Real Estate Equities Co.
Magellan said the transaction will result in a one-time pre-tax loss of $45 million to $55 million in the third quarter.
Under the definitive agreement, Magellan's domestic provider business, Charter Behavioural Health Systems, will be operated as a new 50-50 joint venture, called CBHS, with an affiliate of Crescent.
Crescent, based in Fort Worth, Texas, is one of the nation's largest real estate investment trusts, with a total market capitalisation of more than $2.9 billion.

Magellan will sell substantially all of the hospitals, real estate and related personal property in Charter to Cresent. The venture will operate the facilities under a franchise agreement with Magellan and a lease agreement with Crescent, Magellan said.
Magellan will receive $400 million in cash from Crescent for warrants to buy 1,283,500 Magellan common shares at $30 apiece. The warrants will become exercisable over 12 years, Magellan said.
Magellan, based in Atlanta, will get warrants to buy another 2-1/2 percent of the venture's common stock, and 50 percent of the venture's future earnings.
Magellan will also receive $80 million in yearly franchise fees under the venture agreement, Magellan said.
Magellan will provide the venture with ongoing support in areas that include managed care contracting services, advertising and marketing, the company said.
Magellan's stock rose $2.625 to $26.125, while Crescent edged down 12.5 cents to $52.875, both in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
